reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it presents an ABP News election interview and public political discussion. The free-electricity and public-service statements are attributed to a political speaker and linked to asking for votes, making them campaign promises and electoral advocacy rather than an investment or wealth-return offer. The subscribe prompt concerns ordinary channel engagement, and the described material shows no payment, private-data request, or transaction outcome.

citations.quote: Hello friends you are watching ABP News I am with you, Shobna Yadav.
It is the election on February 8.
When a party comes to the people and says, 'I built a school, so vote. I built a hospital, so vote.'
You're going to have 200 units of electricity free for five years.

opening.argument: The central pitch ties a concrete household benefit to a personal support condition: viewers are told they will receive 200 units of free electricity “as long as you have Kejriwal,” with the period extended to five or ten years depending on continued leadership. The same passage explicitly connects the benefit to asking for a vote. That is a direct promise-action exchange: support the promoter and receive an unusually easy, valuable benefit. The presentation also expands the offer beyond electricity to waived bills, medical care, water, roads and other services, making the solicitation broader than a single policy discussion.

citations.quote: You're going to have 200 units of electricity free as long as you have Kejriwal. You're going to have 200 units of electricity free for five years. You're going to have 10 years until you have me as Chief Minister.
And in the name of development and the Bhatri, you are asking for a vote.
I also paid their electricity bill. I have done free boarding. Someone is sick in your house. I have done his medical care.

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling this an interview does not neutralize the exchange being presented. The speaker himself describes benefits lasting five or ten years and immediately frames them around retaining him in office. The reference side identifies the election setting, but that setting is precisely what makes the promise a solicitation rather than merely neutral reporting.

citations.quote: It is the election on February 8.
You're going to have 200 units of electricity free as long as you have Kejriwal.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The quoted benefits are political promises about public programs, not a viewer reward, private payout, or claimable asset. The accompanying request is plainly a vote, not a click, registration, deposit, purchase, or invitation. The material therefore shows electoral advocacy and policy claims, but it does not show the participation pathway required for a scam offer.

citations.quote: When a party comes to the people and says, 'I built a school, so vote. I built a hospital, so vote.'
And in the name of development and the Bhatri, you are asking for a vote.

opening.argument: Several warning signals appear together: a large recurring household benefit, a simple eligibility condition, a long promised duration, and election timing that creates pressure to act. The speaker says electricity will be free for five years, potentially ten, and presents additional waived bills and services as reasons to support him. These are unusually broad, easy-to-understand returns framed as available through one decisive action: voting for the speaker. Even without a payment request, the combination encourages viewers to treat promised economic relief as a dependable inducement.

fixed your home's electricity bill
When the whole country was in inflation. Then we pardoned the electricity bills of Delhi. We pardoned the water bills of the people of Delhi.
It is the election on February 8.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The news framing does not remove the unusually expansive promises being made on camera. The reference side says there is no transaction outcome, but the concern is the persuasive combination of easy, repeated benefits and a time-bound election context, not merely whether money changes hands during the broadcast.

citations.quote: You're going to have 200 units of electricity free for five years.
It is the election on February 8.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: These statements describe government subsidies and service delivery, not returns generated for participants. The evidence does not show a fee, account, claim link, wallet, investment, or promised cash withdrawal. The election date supplies context for a campaign promise, not proof that the public benefit is a deceptive reward mechanism.

citations.quote: AAP don’t know political games, they only know how to work for the welfare of people.
When a party comes to the people and says, 'I built a school, so vote. I built a hospital, so vote.'

opening.argument: Although packaged as a news program, the segment functions as direct promotion. The interviewer introduces the chief minister before an election, the speaker repeatedly contrasts his record with opponents, and the audience is told that the election is about his work. The studio visuals reinforce that promotional role: the speaker appears in an ABP-branded interview setting, while a large audience watches the event. This is not detached explanation of a benefit; it is a polished public-facing pitch that turns electricity, schools, hospitals and free services into reasons to support one political figure.

citations.quote: Hello friends you are watching ABP News I am with you, Shobna Yadav.
This election is just about the work
When a party comes to the people and says, 'I built a school, so vote. I built a hospital, so vote.'

rebuttal.rebuttal: A broadcaster’s identity and an interview format can make promotion more credible, not less. The segment repeatedly converts alleged services into a request for electoral support, so describing it as discussion overlooks its persuasive function. The reference side also does not answer why the speaker’s benefit claims are repeatedly presented as reasons to act.

citations.quote: This election is just about the work
If this is won, these people will win. They changed the politics of the country.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The visuals and interview format establish a televised political discussion, but they do not establish a scam pathway. The speaker’s own example explicitly uses schools and hospitals as campaign-record arguments, and the requested action is voting. No supplied evidence shows that viewers are asked to pay, register, buy anything, or expect a private financial return.
